concept.name: Stop-limit order
concept.definition: An instruction that becomes a limit order after its stop condition is met, combining a trigger price with an execution-price boundary.
concept.intuition: It is an instruction controlling how an attempt to buy or sell may interact with available liquidity.
concept.mechanics: On trigger, activate the stated buy or sell limit; it may execute at the limit or better, rest unfilled, or expire according to its time in force.
concept.failure_modes: Fast prices, thin depth, venue trigger conventions, and partial fills can produce execution or non-execution different from the displayed quote.
concept.misconceptions: An order's trigger or limit constrains its behavior; it does not guarantee both execution and a particular price.
concept.example: A sell stop-limit with stop $20 and limit $19.50 triggers at $20 but does not fill if the market gaps directly to $19.

citations.source: SEC Office of Investor Education, Trading Basics
citations.section: Market, limit, stop, and stop-limit orders, pp. 1-2
